dod_intent_evidence: Company's own site and news explicitly frame Astraeus for 'satellite defense' and DoD-relevant missions ('Defense ready', 'patrol and protect U.S. assets in orbit, with the ability to intercept threats') — see 'Their own words' technology page and the $8.8M raise news item.
score_evidence: 'Astraeus maneuvers at mission speed, delivering intercept, defense, and repositioning capabilities without delay. Defense ready. Unmatched delta-V.' → lab_language_intensity (spec-sheet bravado, zero operational framing)
Thrust (lbf), Payload Hosting (kg), Delta-v (km/s) stat blocks with no ATO/RMF/DDIL/CMMC/ITAR language anywhere on the site → deployment_awareness_absence

Founding team bios (Ben Schleuniger, Ross Doherty, Nico Montoya) are 100% propulsion/manufacturing engineers from Relativity, Blue Origin, Aerojet — zero mention of operators, warfighters, training, or CONOPS anywhere in the pack → operator_absence

Open roles: 'Head of Business Development' and 'Fluids Design Engineer - Heat Exchangers' — the latter is a neutral domain-engineering hire per calibration rules, but no field/test/integration/compliance role appears → hiring_profile_skew
$8.8M seed raised Aug 2025, founded 2024, 22 employees, still building toward first flight ('The Road to Astraeus' milestones) → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of contested/degraded space command-and-control — the vehicle's tasking and comms links are assumed always-on.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If Astraeus is meant to 'intercept threats' and 'reposition rapidly' during an actual conflict, the adversary jams the C2 uplink and GPS/PNT first — the same DDIL failure mode as ground systems, just applied to space; the site never addresses autonomous or degraded-comms operation.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founding team is entirely propulsion/turbomachinery engineers (Relativity, Blue Origin, Aerojet Rocketdyne) with no visible military-ops or cyber background.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Astraeus maneuvers at mission speed, delivering intercept, defense, and repositioning capabilities without delay.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/STIG or cybersecurity-accreditation language for a vehicle meant to interface with DoD ground stations and command networks.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Flight/tasking software touching military networks needs an Authority to Operate before it can fly a real DoD mission — without RMF/STIG work started early, the promised 'hours not months' response collides with a compliance process that itself runs months to years.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Messaging is aimed at investors/commercial partners (raise announcement, technology specs) rather than at the acquisition/compliance path required to actually fly on a government asset.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: turning months of lead time into hours

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mission-ops, sustainment, or ground-crew hiring or messaging — who tasks, monitors, and maintains a vehicle 'stationed in orbit' 24/7 once fielded.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A persistent in-orbit defense asset still needs a trained mission-ops crew, GFE/SDA-system integration, and an anomaly-response/sustainment plan — none of which appears in hiring or site language; only BD and a heat-exchanger engineering role are open.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company is still pre-launch and hiring for build-out, not operations; ops planning likely hasn't started.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Head of Business Development ... Fluids Design Engineer - Heat Exchangers

opener_hook: Orbital Operations raised $8.8M in August 2025 to build Astraeus, a cryogenic vehicle pitched for satellite defense and threat interception — the two open roles right now are Business Development and a heat-exchanger engineer, with no ops or compliance hire yet.
what_they_do: Builds a high-thrust, cryogenic-propulsion space vehicle (Astraeus) for in-orbit satellite defense, repositioning, and threat interception.
